item.title: U.S. plans to pay $850 million of the $5 billion it owes the United Nations
item.summary: # U.S. plans to pay $850 million of the $5 billion it owes the United Nations - Click here to listen to this article - Share via - The Trump administration plans to send $850 million to the United Nations, a fraction of the roughly $5 billion Washington owes after years of withheld dues as it demands sweeping changes. - The payment, including funds for Haiti and Congo peacekeeping, comes as the U.N. warns of financial strain after a year with no U.S. contributions and deep cuts to global programs. - Some congressional Republicans are balking at the plan, arguing it fails to curb what they call bloated U.N. bureaucracy and does not sufficiently target aid to the Palestinian refugee agency. WASHINGTON — The U.S. government has notified Congress of its plans to pay $850 million of the several billion it owes to the United Nations, the largest payment the Trump administration would make to the world body since it demanded sweeping changes in exchange for continued support as its largest donor.
